pr.title: coverage: Remove `pending_dups` from the span refiner
pr.description:
When extracting coverage spans from a function's MIR, we need to decide how to handle spans that are associated with more than one node (BCB) in the coverage control flow graph.

The existing code for managing those duplicate spans is very subtle and difficult to modify. But by eagerly deduplicating those extracted spans in a much simpler way, we can remove a massive chunk of complexity from the span refiner.

There is a tradeoff here, in that we no longer try to retain *all* nondominating BCBs that have the same span, only the last one in the (semi-arbitrary) dominance ordering. But in practice, this produces very little difference in our coverage tests, and the simplification is so significant that I think it's worthwhile.

analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical change sorts equal `lo`/`hi` spans with closure spans first, then "we want to keep only the most-dominated BCB" via `basic_coverage_blocks.cmp_in_dominator_order(a.bcb, b.bcb).reverse()`, and then runs `initial_spans.dedup_by(|b, a| a.span.source_equal(b.span));`. This eagerly collapses every group of same-source spans to a single span, so only the closure span or the most-dominated BCB survives; all other nondominating duplicate BCBs are discarded before refinement, and the `pending_dups` machinery is removed. This is a simplification with an intentional behavioral tradeoff, not a demonstrated bug fix.
analysis.inputDomain: Coverage-instrumented Rust functions (InstrumentCoverage) whose MIR yields multiple `SpanFromMir` entries with identical source spans but different BasicCoverageBlocks, especially closures produced inside macro expansions and async closures. The supplied regression inputs are `tests/coverage/closure_macro` and `tests/coverage/closure_macro_async`.
analysis.originalLogic: When extracting coverage spans from MIR, `mir_to_initial_sorted_coverage_spans` sorted spans by lo/hi, then by dominator order (dominating BCBs before dominated), then put closure spans first. The `SpansRefiner` kept a `pending_dups` list described as "One or more coverage spans with the same `Span` but different `BasicCoverageBlock`s, and no `BasicCoverageBlock` in this list dominates another `BasicCoverageBlock` in the list." It moved equal-span `prev` into `pending_dups`, retained only dups that do not dominate `curr`, flushed them when safe, and could emit multiple mappings for the same source span. Thus all nondominating BCBs sharing a span were preserved through refinement.
pitfalls: Keeping the wrong representative if closure-first ordering is not applied before `dedup_by`; closure spans must take precedence over non-closure spans
Failing to reverse dominator ordering would keep a dominating BCB instead of the intended most-dominated BCB
Using raw `Span` equality instead of `span.source_equal` changes which macro-expansion spans are considered duplicates
Dropping nondominating duplicate BCBs intentionally changes coverage mappings; the PR itself notes the tradeoff of no longer retaining *all* nondominating BCBs
`dedup_by` only removes adjacent equal elements, so the preceding sort (lo/hi, closure, reversed dominator order) is an invariant of correctness
After removing `pending_dups`, the refiner no longer has a path for overlapping duplicate spans; any same-span group that is not actually collapsed will bypass the old special handling
The final mapping count and raw bytes change (e.g. 7 mappings to 6 in macro closure tests), so test expectations must be updated rather than assuming byte-identical output
preconditions: Building initial coverage spans from MIR via `mir_to_initial_sorted_coverage_spans`
Multiple BCBs map to the same `lo`/`hi` source span
The span group contains a closure span and/or BCBs related by dominance
Spans are fully sorted before dedup so equal-source spans are adjacent
analysis.summary: InstrumentCoverage historically retained multiple coverage spans with the same source span but different nondominating BCBs via `pending_dups`. This PR simplifies the span refiner by eagerly deduplicating same-span covspans: sort closure spans first, then reverse dominator order, then `dedup_by(span.source_equal)`, keeping only one span per identical source span (closure preferred, else most-dominated BCB). The tradeoff is dropping nondominating duplicate BCBs, which changes coverage mappings in macro/closure tests.
analysis.testStrategy: Use InstrumentCoverage coverage tests with closure-in-macro and async-closure inputs (`tests/coverage/closure_macro.*`, `tests/coverage/closure_macro_async.*`). Inspect the generated `.cov-map`: check `Number of file 0 mappings`, the `Raw bytes`, and each `Code(Counter/Expression)` span. Verify that a same-source duplicate pair no longer yields two mappings, that closure spans win over non-closure duplicates, and that the retained BCB is the most-dominated one. Compare against the pre-change expectations to see the intended mapping reductions.
analysis.trigger: Two or more extracted coverage spans have the same source location (`span.source_equal`) but different BCBs, particularly when one is a closure span or when the BCBs are in a dominator relation. Macro-generated closures are the demonstrated trigger in the updated `.cov-map` expectations.
